title: At 11 months, infants looked longer when a toy seemed to pass through a wall
summary: Perez and Feigenson report that 11-month-olds looked longer when a toy appeared to pass through a wall than when the wall stopped it.
body: Jasmin Perez and Lisa Feigenson showed infants a solidity event at about 11 months. A toy rolled behind a screen toward a wall. In the expected outcome the toy was revealed on the near side, as if the wall had stopped it. In the surprising outcome it was on the far side, as if it had passed through. The infants looked longer overall at the surprising outcome, about 6.43 seconds versus 4.99 seconds. The paper was published in PNAS on 28 June 2021, and this card cites the open PMC copy. The result is for the infants in that condition. It is not a statement about most children.

sources.title: Stable individual differences in infants' responses to violations of intuitive physics
sources.author: Jasmin Perez and Lisa Feigenson
sources.note: Peer-reviewed PNAS paper, 28 June 2021, open copy PMC8271639. Paraphrase of the 11-month solidity looking-time result, 6.43 s versus 4.99 s.
